purpose: Qualitative cognitive review of candidate item interpretation before pilot psychometric data collection.

operationalTargets.note: Workflow targets for qualitative review of the v0.6 candidate bank; not psychometric sample-size claims.

interviewSequence.prompt: Answer the item as you normally would before discussing it.
In your own words, what is this item asking?
What were you thinking about when you chose your answer?
Were any words or phrases unclear, technical, loaded, or open to more than one meaning?
Could someone reasonably interpret this item in a different way? If so, how?
Did the available response options let you express your actual view?
Did any response feel socially expected, embarrassing, virtuous, extreme, or otherwise pressured?
If you chose a midpoint or special response, what did that response mean to you in this case?
How, if at all, would you rewrite the item to make your interpretation clearer without changing the idea?

requirements: Minimum independent cognitive-review target reached for the exact item revision.
No unresolved major comprehension or branching issue.
No unresolved ideological-cue or response-option defect.
Reviewer paraphrases substantially converge on the intended construct meaning.
Any revision triggered by review increments the item revision and resets review counts for the changed wording.
promotionGate.note: Passing cognitive review permits pilot testing only; it does not establish reliability, validity, invariance, or calibrated scoring.
